findings.summary: Boston magazine identifies Hicham as Sam Hassan and describes Tarek and Talal as his nephews
findings.detail: January 16, 2019 reporting associates Hicham/Sam with The Tannery, dates the first Cambridge store to 1973, and reports Beirut birth in 1949. The nephew links and early history are attributed reporting; civil records were not retrieved in this track.

findings.summary: Reported early Tannery finance includes Frye trade credit and claimed Reebok credit lines
findings.detail: The initiating article attributes early Frye credit and a claimed $1 million Reebok credit limit per store to Hassan. No facility agreement, draw history or transfer into real estate was retrieved. These are testable ordinary financing leads, not established sources of all family wealth.

findings.summary: Talal Hassan identifies Tarek as his brother and recounts a retail career from Tannery to Trend Boston
findings.detail: In a December 1, 2025 first-person retrospective attributed to Talal, he describes growing up in a Beirut retail family, starting in The Tannery stockroom in 1984, and opening Trend Boston in 2016. This supports the reported sibling relationship and personal account of business origins; no named paternal funding source or capital amount is supplied. A separate Tarek profile also names Talal as his brother. The corporate vehicle and Trend opening date require filing corroboration.

findings.summary: Concepts identifies Tarek Hassan as its founder and dates its Cambridge start to 1996
findings.detail: The first-party CNCPTS site names Tarek Hassan as founder, Cambridge Massachusetts as origin, and 1996 as founding year. This is a business-origin statement, not evidence of current equity percentages. Trade interviews connect that origin to The Tannery; the full legal-name/business link remains subject to corporate and litigation cross-checks.

findings.summary: 2018 reporting describes a Concepts investment from Zappos with undisclosed terms
findings.detail: Hypebeast reported in August 2018 that Concepts confirmed investment from Zappos and quoted a statement from Tarek Hassan, CEO of Concepts International. The reviewed text does not identify the amount, percentage, precise purchasing legal entity or use of proceeds. This is a reported outside-capital lead; it does not establish funds moved into Hassan real estate or personal wealth.

findings.summary: Trend Boston describes family retail roots and lists two Newbury Street stores
findings.detail: The first-party About page describes more than 40 years of experience in a family-owned shoe business and lists stores at 134 and 351 Newbury Street as observed September 4, 2026. BBB separately lists Talal Hassan as manager at 134 Newbury and a January 1, 2017 business start. Talal dates opening to 2016 in his retrospective; neither date has yet been verified from original filings. Store locations do not prove title.

findings.summary: FEC record dated November 6, 1992 lists Hicham Ali Hassan of Hull with employer Tannery and a $500 contribution
findings.detail: The official FEC Schedule A API returns contributor_name HASSAN, HICHAM ALI; contributor_city HULL; contributor_state MA; contributor_employer TANNERY; receipt date 1992-11-06; amount 500.0; committee C00174862 (Committee to Re-Elect Senator Edward M Kennedy); sub_id 3061920110003101283; image 93020012770. Exact multi-part name plus the Tannery business affiliation support identity resolution. Later employer-matched rows run through 1998. Raw results contain multiple rows sharing date, amount and image; no aggregate donation total is asserted. The record establishes a reported employer/business link and political contribution, not source of wealth or influence. Durable API record: investigations/hassan-boston/evidence/disclosures/fec-hicham-1.json.

findings.summary: July 2022 Massachusetts campaign report identifies Houssam Hassan as Developer/Owner at Silverstone Development
findings.detail: OCPF Composite Depository Bank Report for Campbell, Andrea Joy (CPF ID 15931), reporting period 2022-07-01 to 2022-07-31, filed 2022-08-02, lists Hassan, Houssam as an individual donor, Developer/Owner, Silverstone Development, a $300 credit-card receipt dated 2022-07-18. Source PDF page 23; city continues on page 24. The source business address matches the official Massachusetts PEMBROKE TOWNHOUSE LLC (001037265) record identifying HOUSSAM ALI HASSAN as resident agent and manager; this provides a second contextual identifier. Corporate evidence maintained by Track B at evidence/corporate/entity-001037265.txt. Source occupation/employer fields are reported declarations, not independent proof of equity ownership. Address is retained in original evidence for disambiguation and omitted from public-facing summary. Durable PDF and visually reviewed page: evidence/disclosures/ocpf-841345.pdf and ocpf-page-23.png.

findings.summary: Massachusetts AG amended complaint identifies Hicham Ali Hassan as Sam Hassan and sues him individually
findings.detail: The September 21, 2018 amended complaint in Commonwealth v Hicham Ali Hassan, Suffolk Superior 18-2285E, identifies him as owner/manager of The Tannery at 711 Boylston and states individual capacity. This is an official pleading identification, distinct from proving its misconduct allegations.

findings.summary: 2021 consent judgment imposed public-accommodation operating injunction and $220,000 obligation, half suspended
findings.detail: Commonwealth v Hicham Ali Hassan, Suffolk Superior 18-2285E / 1884CV02285. Signed judgment dated August 13, 2021, visually verified on PDF p8. Section I.C permanently bars operating any Massachusetts public accommodation; operating is defined as control or participation in business activities relating to customer/potential customer interactions. Section II requires $110,000 within five business days of entry and suspends a further $110,000 to secure compliance. Section IV waives findings/adjudication and states no admission or evidence of liability in other proceedings. Do not treat as a trial finding or proof the immediate payment was made. AG announcement dated August 27, 2021.

findings.summary: 2020 family-property opinion recounts alleged 2000 buyout and retained minority interests
findings.detail: Tarek Ali Hassan v Hicham Ali Hassan et al, Suffolk Superior BLS 2020CV0531-BLS2, July23 2020: complaint allegations assumed true only for pleading motions. Court recounts a December14 2000 Settlement Agreement under which Hicham would purchase family interests while Tarek retained 5% beneficial interests in three trusts and director/minority-shareholder positions in two corporations. Named exactly as printed: 376 Boston Street Realty Trust; 4000 Boylston Street Realty Trust; Eighteen Brimmer Street Realty Trust; 419 Boylston Street Corporation; 216-218 Newbury Street Corporation. First two names may contain typographical errors and are not normalized as title evidence. Opinion calls Hicham Tarek's uncle, says unnamed father and other family members held interests. Original agreement/exhibits and later disposition required; this motion decision did not adjudicate ownership.

findings.summary: Court allowed Tarek property claims to proceed and dismissed Hicham counterclaims at pleading stage in 2020
findings.detail: Same Suffolk BLS case. Defendants' limitations motion for judgment on the pleadings denied; Tarek's motion to dismiss counterclaims allowed July23 2020. Counterclaims alleged diversion of goods/cash, including an amount exceeding $700,000 for 2012-14 purportedly found in a 2016 audit; these are allegations, not established facts. Court applied three-year tort limitation, noted other pleading defects, and ordered counterclaims dismissed. No ultimate finding on the merits of Tarek's beneficial-interest claim is made by this order.

findings.summary: 2020 court opinion reports earlier Staff USA unpaid-invoice litigation had recently settled
findings.detail: July23 2020 Tarek v Hicham opinion identifies Staff USA, Inc. v Paloma LLC d/b/a The Tannery, Suffolk Superior 1784CV0624-D, as a 2017 unpaid-invoice action and states Tarek was also named defendant. Court says docket showed it recently settled. This is a primary judicial account of related litigation; original docket and settlement amounts not retrieved. Source spelling Paloma LLC retained, candidate association to registered Paloma Tannery LLC requires entity context.

findings.summary: 2010 appellate decision ordered Boylston property conveyance following $4.5 million offer
findings.detail: Fienberg v Hassan, 77 Mass. App. Ct. 901, 09-P-1545, June16 2010. Andrew Fienberg as trustee of Aidee Realty Trust owned 382-390 Boylston; Rattlesnake Bar & Grill Inc held right of first refusal. Opinion records May14 2008 Hassan offer of $4.5m with $500k deposit paid with offer, accepted by Fienberg, and May22 purchase-and-sale agreement. Appeals Court reversed trial judgment because Rattlesnake offer materially differed in timing and remanded to order conveyance to Hassan. This is a contract/judicial-order record; deed and source of deposit/final funds remain to be traced.

findings.summary: Nader bankruptcy schedules report zero assets and $2.50 million corporate liabilities in July 2017
findings.detail: Nader Corp, Massachusetts bankruptcy 17-12398, document9 filed July10 2017. Summary reports assets $0, secured claims $0, priority unsecured claims $986,207.26 and nonpriority unsecured claims $1,513,827.76; total $2,500,035.02. Priority amounts are two listed IRS corporate-income-tax claims ($689,586.55 for June30 2011 and $296,620.71 for June30 2012). Debtor reports are not an adjudication of claims or personal net worth. Hicham signed as president. Schedule H includes overlapping Alana/Paloma obligations, so summing corporation liabilities would double-count shared debts.

findings.summary: Nader financial-affairs statement reports Hicham as 100% shareholder and identifies accounting and factoring contacts
findings.detail: Nader 17-12398 doc9 p30 names Hicham Ali Hassan President/Treasurer/Secretary/Director with 100% interest. P29 names Cain, Bourret, Jarry & Associates and Andrew Baxter as accountants/bookkeepers and record custodians; financial statements sent to Hildun Corporation and CitiGroup/Commercial Services. P24 reports zero gross revenue in 2015,2016 and 2017-to-filing. These are sworn debtor disclosures at a point in time, not independent audited results. They supply ordinary trade-credit/accounting leads for operating-versus-property entity reconciliation.

findings.summary: Nader schedules identify Alana, Paloma and Hicham co-obligor links, including possible Gucci guarantee
findings.detail: Nader 17-12398 doc9 Schedule H lists Alana Inc as codebtor for 31 creditor entries, Paloma Tannery LLC for six (Adidas America, ArcTeryx, Staff USA, Valentino USA, CIT Group Commercial, Colliers Int'l N.E. LLC), and Hicham for Gucci and Stuart Weitzman. Gucci entry specifically says Possible personal guarantee; underlying guaranties were not retrieved and personal enforceability/current balances not established. Scheduled vendor amounts include Gucci $56,959, Stuart Weitzman $73,847, Colliers $289,716.58, Staff $136,151.70, Valentino $175,557.96.

findings.summary: Nader statement lists Gucci collection case naming Hicham and both bankrupt corporations
findings.detail: Nader 17-12398 doc9 p25 lists Gucci America, Inc. v Alana Inc dba The Tannery, Nader Inc dba The Tannery and Hicham Ali Hassan, Suffolk Superior case 170038E. Debtor labels nature collection; exact standardized docket and final disposition remain unresolved. The same page lists IRS audit completed May9 2016. Personal co-defendant status does not establish personal judgment or debt amount.

findings.summary: 2026 ADA website complaint names Trend Boston as defendant and Talal Ali Hassan as registered agent
findings.detail: Sophia Faldonie v Trend Boston LLC, D.Mass.1:26-cv-11306-LTS, filed March17 2026, alleges inaccessible trendboston.com under ADA TitleIII and requests injunctive/declaratory relief, fees, costs and statutory damages without a specified amount. Paragraph15 identifies defendant as Massachusetts LLC at 134 Newbury Street with Talal Ali Hassan as registered agent. Talal is not a named defendant. RECAP index later records May14 2026 notice of settlement and 60-day settlement dismissal; no liability adjudication or settlement amount reviewed.

findings.summary: Federal Collymore discrimination pleading survived dismissal motion; docket later marked terminated
findings.detail: Collymore v Tannery and Hicham Ali Hassan a/k/a Sam Hassan, D.Mass.1:18-cv-11634-LTS. January8 2019 order denied Tannery motion to dismiss amended complaint, finding allegations sufficient at pleading stage under 42 USC1981; the order is not a liability finding. CourtListener docket metadata records filed August3 2018 (opinion narrative says complaint August2) and termination January28 2019. Termination disposition and terms were not in the retrieved docket documents; do not label settlement or merits outcome.

findings.summary: Andrew Fienberg, as successor trustee of Aidee Realty Trust, conveyed 384–390 Boylston Street to Hicham as trustee for $4.5 million in 2011.
findings.detail: Original Suffolk declaration 47449/1 and acquisition deed 47449/6 were visually reviewed in full. Hicham Ali Hassan of Boston executed the five-page declaration on January 4, 2011 as original sole trustee of the 384 Boylston Street Realty Trust. The declaration calls it a nominee trust and places beneficiary identities and proportions in a separate Schedule of Beneficial Interest filed with the trustee; that schedule is not included in the recorded declaration. Andrew Fienberg, also written Andrew Feinberg in the deed, acting as successor trustee of the Aidee Realty Trust dated September 9, 1959 at 7425/114, executed the two-page quitclaim deed on January 6, 2011. It conveyed the parcel numbered 384–390 Boylston Street to Hicham solely as trustee of the 384 trust for $4,500,000. Both instruments were recorded January 7, 2011. The two reviewed originals do not identify a mortgage, purchase-fund source, or the trust beneficiaries; no negative conclusion is drawn about separate instruments not yet searched in that recording session.

findings.summary: MERS discharged mortgage 34623/310 on 4 Pinecrest Road
findings.detail: Plymouth discharge 34869/46, document 76368, was executed July 17, 2007 by Roxanne Bermea as MERS Assistant Secretary and recorded July 27, 2007. MERS, as holder, acknowledged satisfaction of mortgage 34623/310, document 56456, from Houssam Ali Hassan. Exact book, page and document identifiers establish the link. The discharge does not state the cash paid or prior balance.
